document_title: Fairbanks Would Size a Data Center Like an 800-Seat Venue
post_copy:
The size line Fairbanks staff propose for data centers matches the code's rule for an entertainment facility with 800 or more seats.
Both say 40,000 square feet.

That rule covers building aesthetics, maintenance and parking lot design. Staff say commenters want rules on water and air quality and on power and noise.

Ordinance 2026-42 would pause land use permits for large-scale data centers through the end of 2027. Staff support it. The Planning Commission hears it Tuesday, November 10th at 6 p.m.

Two of the ordinance's three tests already measure power. Section 4 orders a study of nearly the same list.

One illustrated building, drawn nine ways. The amendment on its floor, the ruler it borrows, the outside that ruler covers, the inside it doesn't, and what happens after Tuesday.

Is a venue's number good enough to stand in until the study reports?

#Fairbanks #DataCenters #Zoning
deck_summary_line: One illustrated building, drawn nine ways. The amendment on its floor, the ruler it borrows, the outside that ruler covers, the inside it doesn't, and what happens after Tuesday.

slides.headline: A data center, sized like an 800-seat venue.
Staff back the pause and a 40,000 size line.
slides.body: Ordinance 2026-42 would bar land use permits for large-scale data centers through December 31st, 2027. Planning staff recommend approval with two amendments. Count gross floor area, and cut the size trigger from 50,000 to 40,000 square feet.
labels: 50,000 SQ FT, THE TRIGGER AS WRITTEN

slides.headline: The new line is borrowed from the code's big-venue rule.
slides.body: Title 18 already defines large scale development. An entertainment facility counts past 40,000 square feet with 800 or more seats. Staff expect data centers to be similar in size and impact.
labels: THOUSAND SQ FT OF FLOOR AREA

slides.headline: The borrowed rule covers the outside.
slides.body: Title 18 standards for large scale development address building aesthetics, maintenance and parking lot design. According to the staff report, commenters want rules for water and air quality, power and water supply, noise, vibrations and size.

slides.headline: "Our largest concern is that nobody asked us."
labels: SARAH HOLLISTER, WHO HELPED ORGANIZE AN OCTOBER 29TH FAIRBANKS TOWN HALL ON DATA CENTERS
ABOUT 150 CAME, PER ALASKA'S NEWS SOURCE. ORGANIZERS SAY NEARLY 200.

slides.kicker: FROM THE STAFF REPORT AND DRAFT PLAN
slides.headline: Same shell. Servers instead of pallets.
slides.body: Borough code has no definition for a data center and lists it as a use in no zone. Warehouse, a use staff say may be similar, is listed in three. The draft plan calls data centers warehouse-type facilities.

slides.headline: Two of its three tests measure power.
slides.body: A data center is large at 5 MW of peak demand, at 5 MW of onsite generation, or past the floor area line. Section 4 orders a study of energy, air, water and noise, due within six months.

slides.headline: Tuesday recommends. The Assembly hears it later.
slides.body: Staff cite a precedent. After the 2014 vote that legalized marijuana facilities, licensing took about 18 months and worked as a de facto moratorium.
labels: NOVEMBER 10TH · COMMISSION HEARS G.3, THEN G.4
WEEKS LATER, USUALLY · ASSEMBLY HEARING, NO DATE SET
DECEMBER 31ST, 2027 · ENDS UNLESS THE ASSEMBLY ACTS
STUDY · SIX MONTHS FROM THE EFFECTIVE DATE

slides.headline: Square feet or megawatts. Which should decide "large" in Fairbanks?

aftercare: Post before the hearing. Tuesday to Thursday 8 to 11 a.m. AKT are the strongest slots, and the Planning Commission hears Ordinance 2026-42 on Tuesday, November 10th at 6 p.m., so Tuesday morning is the useful window (Monday the 9th works if you want it out a day ahead). Drafts arrive daily and you own the cadence.
Paste the sources comment within 60 seconds of posting.

Reply to every comment in the first 60 to 90 minutes. If someone asks about testifying, the agenda's citizens' comments period is three minutes, but no time limit was verified for the G.4 hearing testimony, so don't promise one.
After the hearing on November 10th, slides 02 and 08 and the caption describe the record before the vote. Answer with the commission's outcome in a reply and leave the post as it is.
Note saves and comments at 48 hours.
editor_notes_for_email: The building in the art is illustrative: no site, applicant or size has been filed, and the record holds only inquiries. Nothing has been voted; staff recommend and the commission hears it Tuesday. The record gives two referral dates (October 22nd on the ordinance, October 26th in the staff report), and the deck prints neither. The town hall is not tied to the ordinance on any surface.
